contracts.name: EcoFuturesAdmin
contracts.title: EcoFuturesAdmin -- who is who
contracts.notice: Identity and standing for every actor, and the protocol directory. It holds no money. Trust Admins (Holders) admitted, removed and replaced only by Council vote, through Governance Verifiers admitted by a Holder of their own country, in organisations bound to ONE Holder Standing suspension and dismissal of verifiers; the freeze of a Holder (Governance) Identity the automated identity check (the server marks it): one record per person links all of that person's wallets. GTAs, Holders and verifiers pass it before they are admitted; a patron passes it to buy (FM p2) Organisations the unit of independence: a person belongs to one at a time. A verifier who moves gets a new wallet in the new organisation; the old one keeps its seats but takes no new work, and the person never challenges, attests, claims or is reseated on its former organisation's covenants. A country needs two organisations before its first verification (FM p6) Agreements the digital agreements each party accepted, by hash
contracts.dev: HOLDER SUCCESSION. When the Council replaces a Holder, the old Holder's successor takes its fee and its authority over every covenant at once (Lifecycle v5 §12). Nothing is migrated: the verifier keeps its admitting Holder, and holderOf() follows the line to whoever holds it now. Only a replaced Holder has a successor, so the line is short and acyclic by construction.

contracts.name: EcoCountries
contracts.title: EcoCountries -- the rulebook: countries, their settings, and the flows they follow
contracts.notice: What a request in each country must go through and what it costs. THE FLOW, per country, as data: an ordered list of Steps, validated when it is defined. A country's five settings (Lifecycle v5 §5) are a flow id (registration timing and the power), the term limits and the listing window, plus the window after a sale for path B's recording. For example: Sri Lanka, path A, under a power POWER, POWER_ANCHOR, DEED, ATTEST, MINT, SALE Japan, path A DEED, ATTEST, MINT, SALE Brazil, path B DEED, ATTEST, MINT, SALE, RECORDING, ATTEST WHO CHANGES WHAT. The Foundation defines flows and enables a country with its first settings. After that a Trust Admin of the country proposes new settings, with the hash of counsel's note on the new law, and the Council decides by a majority of all seats (§5). A change applies only to requests made after it. Prices are not legal settings: a Trust Admin of the country, or a GTA, sets them directly.

contracts.name: EcoRegistry
contracts.title: EcoRegistry -- every request, from the guardian's payment to its covenant's activation
contracts.notice: THE FIXED HEAD, the same in every country (1 Oct 2026): requestVerification -> claim -> submitVerification -> watchdog window (challengeable) THEN THE COUNTRY'S FLOW (EcoCountries), one step at a time. EcoDeeds records each power, document and attestation and reports it here; the guardian mints; the Bank reports the sale. A covenant is active when its flow completes: at the sale in path A, at the recording's attestation in path B, which is why the price waits in the Bank's escrow between the two. THE MONEY HERE is the landowner's upfront payment (FM p9), held per request in three parts and paid as the work is done. Each part is zeroed when it is paid, and whatever is left when a request ends goes back to the landowner, so this contract's balance always equals the sum of what its requests still hold. verifierShare the verification fee, V x (1 + sqrt ha) -> the verifier at the first attestation, or when the landowner refuses to sign or abandons attestationFee the attestation fee, V -> the attester of the flow's last document judgmentFee D x (1.5 + sqrt ha) -> the watchdog-1 judges; otherwise the verifier when the watchdog window passes A request that ends any other way -- no claim, W1B upheld, the Deed not anchored, a failed attestation -- refunds the landowner.

contracts.name: EcoDeeds
contracts.title: EcoDeeds -- the paper trail
contracts.notice: The digital mirror of every paper event in a covenant's flow (Lifecycle v5 §2): each document's hash, date and registration number, and the independent attester who confirms that the paper and its mirror match. The Registry holds the request, its money and its place in the flow; this contract records the evidence and tells the Registry when a step is done. power the Trust Admin grants the request's verifier a power of attorney for this land, one land per power (1 Oct 2026), recorded from the Trust Admin's own wallet; then the registered power is recorded with its registration number document the verifier or the Trust Admin records the agreement, the deed or its recording; until it is attested it may be recorded again, to correct it attest one independent person confirms the document against the register, and the power where there is one. A test, not a challenge (1 Oct 2026). WHO ATTESTS (FM p12): a verifier of another organisation than the land's verifier, or a Trust Admin of the country other than the land's; from day 21 of the attestation clock, also a GTA. The attester uploads the registry's certified copy and folio extract and records the registration. THE CLOCKS (FM p4-5, p12-13), each from the moment its step became current: power 7 days to sign, a notice, 7 more: then the Council may move the land to another Holder anchoring 14 days to anchor the signed Deed (or agreement); extensions of 14 from the Holder and 14 from the Council. From day 7 the landowner or the Holder may anchor it. Not anchored in time: the request lapses and everything goes back to the landowner. The landowner's refusal to sign, recorded by the verifier, ends it too -- the verifier keeps its verification fee. attestation 30 days; extensions of 30 from the Holder and 30 from the Council. Not attested in time: the request lapses, everything back to the landowner. A corrected document restarts the clock. An extension is asked before the deadline, with its cause; the Holder decides the first within 3 days, and silence counts as granted; the second is the Council's; there is no third.

contracts.name: EcoChallenge
contracts.title: EcoChallenge -- challenges, the review windows and the review pool
contracts.notice: THE MENU (Covenant Flow Map v25, p15-17). A challenger picks one option and lodges its evidence in the same transaction; the option alone decides what an upheld verdict does. watchdog 1 (the request, after its verification) W1A the verification is wrong upheld: the verifier is removed and flagged; the request goes back to unclaimed, the challenger with a 3-day first claim W1B the land cannot be covenanted upheld: the request ends and the landowner is refunded; the verifier is flagged the term (the covenant) T3A the Deed is not on the register blocked; the last attester loses its fee and is flagged; the Holder has 60 days to restore it, or the covenant closes early T3B the score is wrong the verifier loses the seat and is flagged; held until the new verifier re-verifies, then back-paid at the corrected score T3C natural damage a re-verification falls due within 14 days; no flag T3D a landowner breach blocked until the cure is re-verified; no flag T3E the block is wrong (the landowner) the block is lifted and the held amounts released; the verifier is flagged dismissed (any option): nothing changes; the challenger is flagged, unless it is the landowner a lapse or a withdrawal: no flag WHO RAISES: W1A-T3D, any verifier in standing of the country from another organisation than the land's verifier -- under the same Holder or not; T3E, only the landowner. One undecided challenge per subject at a time. T3A and T3B concern the verification and its review window, so they are raised inside an open window; T3C-T3E at any time in the term. WHO DECIDES: three judges drawn from the country's Trust Admins, excluding the covenant's own, the Trust Admins of both parties' organisations and any frozen one; GTAs fill the seats too few remain for. Two matching votes decide, upheld or dismissed. The clock: 7 days to answer, 7 for the verdict, one redraw of 7 -- 21 days from the raise; then it lapses, as dismissed, with no flag. THE REVIEW WINDOW: 30 days after each re-verification. An outside party attests it with the registry's new certified copy (a verifier of another organisation, a Trust Admin of the country other than the land's, or from day 21 a GTA): one act's fee at the close, and the unattested count resets. Three windows in a row unattested halt instalment releases until an attestation. THE REVIEW POOL is 1% of the sale, held here: one act's fee per scheduled window (the pool / the review acts). A decided term challenge is paid one act's fee: upheld 60% to the challenger and 40% to the judges, dismissed 40% to the judges; what is unpaid stays in the pool, and its remainder goes to the landowner after the End Date.

contracts.notice: The GTAs are the Council. Its decisions are made on chain: a GTA proposes an action, GTAs approve it, and it executes once a majority of ALL seats has approved (§3.1, §5). What the Council decides: ADD_GTA, REMOVE_GTA its own membership (the GTA being removed does not count) ADMIT_HOLDER Trust Admins (a Holder's replacement is a country vote: see below) FREEZE_HOLDER, UNFREEZE_HOLDER a Trust Admin's freeze; RATIFY_FREEZE keeps an emergency freeze SET_COUNTRY_STATUS suspending or resuming a country REVOKE_POWER recording a power's revocation; an unauthorised one freezes the Holder SWITCH_PAYEE the payee when land changes hands or heirship is proven (§10) REASSIGN_VERIFIER moving a request to another of its Trust Admin's verifiers CLEAR_PARCEL releasing a parcel hash UNBLOCK_COVENANT, CANCEL_ the consequences a GTA reviews but never effects alone: unblocking, COVENANT, NOMINATE_VERIFIER, cancelling and reseating a covenant whose Trust Admin cannot act, the drip FREEZE_DRIP, SUSPEND_VERIFIER, valve, and a verifier's suspension or dismissal DISMISS_VERIFIER END_REWARD, EXTEND_CLOCK, fraud's end of TR3, a clock's second extension, a compulsory acquisition ACQUISITION CANCEL_ROOT cancelling an operation queued on the root's 7-day timelock (U3) RECORD_DOCUMENT the Articles, an authorisation, a certificate (G10) COUNTRY VOTES -- the GTAs and the country's own Holders (not frozen), by more than half of them -- decide a Holder's replacement (FM p19, G3: it removes the Holder and names its Successor in the same country, whose fee and authority over every covenant follow at once), the country's fees and execution allowance, and its module settings on a Holder's proposal with counsel's note (Ravi, 10 Oct: "based on GTA + TA (local only) vote"). contracts.name: Tree
contracts.title: Tree -- TR3, the TREE reward, and the Overcharge Reserve
contracts.notice: An ERC-20 minted only by claims against what protected land has released. The rules are the Covenant Flow Map v25 (p10-11), the TR3 Final Model v6 and the Overcharge & Reserve addendum, all 9 Oct 2026. EDITIONS. 21 editions on the Fibonacci numbers, each minting at most 10,000,000 TR3: at most 210,000,000 TR3 ever exist. Where a land stands in them -- its reservation in the request queue, the edition fixed at its auction, its sale -- is EcoEditions' (V12.1, Ravi's change note of 13 Oct). At the sale's completion this contract takes the land's allocation from there (its land-years at the fixed edition's rate) and starts its stream. THE STREAM. A covenant's allocation (its land-years at the edition's rate) accrues evenly over its term and is released when each re-verification passes: what accrued since the last pass, at the score in force since then. Nothing is held back. At each release the score's shortfall -- allocation x (100 - score) / 100 -- goes to the Overcharge Reserve. The split never changes: patron (the EFT's owner) 90%, landowner 10% of which the referrer takes 30%; a verifier, Trust Admin or GTA referrer takes nothing and its share stays with the landowner. CLAIMS (R, 14 Oct). The patron's share of each release waits in the EFT's pool until the EFT's owner claims it; a sale passes the pool, and the rest of the stream, to the buyer, and nothing is minted at a transfer. Only the owner makes the patron claim. Anyone may trigger the guardian claim, which mints the landowner's and the referrer's shares and never touches the pool. Every event that changes what the EFT carries -- a patron claim, a release, a boost, an end -- voids the EFT's open orders (EcoFuturesToken.voidOrders); a guardian claim does not. PAUSES AND ENDS (Core reports each): missed re-verification each day past due + grace credits its full allocation to the Reserve a hold (breach, a Deed off the register, a wrong score) nothing is released until the hold lifts; then the backlog is released -- at the corrected score when the hold was for a wrong score (option 3B) an early end everything not yet released goes to the Reserve; capacity never reopens the End Date the last release; anything still held goes to the Reserve THE OVERCHARGE RESERVE is a counter, never a balance: nothing is minted into it. Boosts (EcoOvercharge) draw on it, first come first served. After the last edition has closed and the last term has ended, anyone may finalise it, which burns what is left. A BOOST (EcoOvercharge applies a Relic): M = F(target) / F(Relic), kept x 1e6. The commit -- the least of the remaining allocation x (M - 1), the Relic's cap and the Reserve -- leaves the Reserve at once. Each release then pays what was released x (M - 1) from the commit, so the boost follows the live score; whatever the commit has not paid when the stream ends returns to the Reserve. A boost never uses edition capacity.

The target must be live and unheld -- not blocked, frozen or held for any reason -- and is overcharged once. The Flow Map (later than the addendum) lets an EFT be overcharged after TR3 has been claimed; the boost applies to the allocation still to stream. TRANSMUTATION burns two Relics of the same edition (2 or later) for one Relic an edition lower, whose cap is the sum of theirs.

contracts.name: EcoEditions
contracts.title: EcoEditions -- the editions and the request queue
contracts.notice: Where every land stands in the 21 editions, from its request to its sale. Ravi's change note of 13 Oct 2026, "Edition placement by request queue" (docs/design/V12_1_Edition_Queue.md); Tree keeps the streams. EDITIONS. Edition n holds SCALE x Fn^2 land-years (1,000 x Fn^2 hectare-years in production) and mints at most 10,000,000 TR3: 10,000 / Fn^2 TR3 per hectare-year at a score of 100. A title may take at most 100 x Fn hectare-years in edition n (10,000 x Fn land-years). Each edition counts its capacity C, what is reserved R and what is sold S, with S <= R <= C. THE QUEUE (rules 1, 6). A paid request takes the next place in one queue for every country -- its request id, issued in payment order -- and reserves its land-years in the LOWEST edition with room for all of it whose limit it fits: its provisional edition. Space a release frees in an edition goes first, in queue order, to the earliest waiting request in a higher edition that fits it (promote, permissionless; the contract checks the order); that frees space higher up, so it cascades. A request never moves up. Freed space is held back from new requests until settle shows no waiting request can use it. FIXED AT THE AUCTION'S END (rules 7, 8). The Market fixes a request's edition when its auction ends with a winner, and unfixes it when that sale is called off (a failed KYC; path B's refund to relist): the reservation stays. At the sale's completion Tree sells it: S grows, and the allocation is its land-years at the fixed edition's rate (capped at 1,000,000 TR3; the excess burned). A reservation holds space, never TR3: a release credits nothing to the Reserve. CLOSING (rule 9). An edition closes when all its space is sold, or eight protocol years after it opens. Editions open one after another: edition 1 at the deploy, each next when the one below closes (at the clock's mark when the clock closed it). A higher edition may hold reservations before it opens; its clock waits. At a close the space no request has reserved is burned, and so is a reservation released after it.
